model_annotation: This chart is a nested donut (ring) chart consisting of two concentric rings that represent two different measures of ambiguity: "Ambiguity Std" on the outer ring and "Max Ambiguity" on the inner ring. The outer ring is divided into four slices corresponding to different standard deviation values. The largest slice, labeled "Std: 0.0," appears in a very dark navy/teal color and accounts for 49.0% of the outer ring. The next slice, "Std: 0.47," is shown in a dark blue and represents 47.7%. The third slice, "Std: 0.94," is depicted in a medium-light blue at 7.0%, and the fourth slice, "Std: 0.82," appears in a medium dark teal-blue at 5.0%, with these two smaller slices positioned at the top-right of the ring. The inner ring is divided into three slices representing maximum ambiguity values. The largest inner slice, "Max: 2," is shown in a medium sky blue and accounts for 39.0%. The next slice, "Max: 1," appears in a slightly darker cyan-blue at 38.0%. The smallest inner slice, "Max: 3," is depicted in a very light/pale blue at 14.2%, positioned at the bottom-right of the inner ring. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice. Two separate legends are provided to the right of the chart, one for each ring, clearly distinguishing the color coding for the outer "Ambiguity Std" categories and the inner "Max Ambiguity" categories. No slices appear to be visually exploded or offset from the rings.
